### Page 88

[88]
GPU 수요를 직접 설계하는 엔비디아
엔비디아의 4가지 네오클라우드 지원 방식
▪ 엔비디아는 ① 지분투자, ② 코로케이션 계약 확보, ③ 컨소시엄 구성, ④ 보증·백스톱을 통해 GPU 수요를 직접 설계
▪ 지분투자: CoreWeave, Nebius 등 주요 네오클라우드에 직접 출자해 조달 여력과 신용도를 보강
▪ 코로케이션 계약 확보: 병목인 물리 인프라를 직접 계약으로 선점한 뒤 네오클라우드에 재임대
▪ 컨소시엄 구성: 금융사와 약 5,000억달러 규모의 제3자 자본 유치 플랫폼을 조성
▪ 보증·백스톱: GPU 담보대출 잔존가치 보증(손실분의 25%), 미판매 용량은 정해진 요율로 재임차 약정

Investment Point
▪ 한국판 Stargate의 중심에서 대규모 AIDC 사업 확대: 글로벌 AI 고객 수
요·자본을 SK하이퍼의 개발 역량과 결합해 코로케이션·GPU Cloud 및 전
력 인프라를 확대. 제도 개방 시 AIDC에 전력을 조달·판매하고, 장기적으

로 공장·대형 빌딩까지 B2B 공급 대상을 넓히는 AI 유틸리티로 확장 가능
▪ 전력사업 개방을 AIDC의 적기 가동으로 연결하는 SK하이퍼: 한전의 전력
망 투자 부담과 계통접속 지연으로 민간의 인프라 개발 참여 필요성 증가.
Hyper는 발전사와의 전원 협의, 한전의 접속 검토, 인입선로·변전소 구축
을 DC 개발 일정과 조율하며, 확대되는 민간 참여 기회를 실제 사업으로
구현하는 핵심 주체
▪ 5GW 전량 가동 시 SKT 지배순이익 약 4,631억원 기여 추정: 코로케이션
3GW와 GPU Cloud 2GW, 프로젝트 순이익 전액 배당, Hyper의 사업법
인 지분 10% 및 SKT의 Hyper 지분 100% 유지 가정. 기여액은 통상 순
이익 약 1.3조원의 36%에 해당하는 규모. 별도로 Horizon도 2030년
314MW, 매출 1조원·영업이익 1,500억원을 가정해 기존 DC 사업의 이

익 기반 확대
▪ 투자의견 BUY, 목표주가 135,700원 상향 조정: 2027년 예상 지배 EPS
6,785원에 목표 PER 20배(Softbank Corp FY27 PER)를 적용. 통신과
전력판매를 함께 영위하는 일본 SoftBank Corp(9434.JP)를 피어로 선정
했으며, AIDC 개발과 기업용 전력공급으로의 사업 확장 잠재력을 감안하
면 동등한 수준의 멀티플 적용이 가능하다고 판단함
▪ 현재 시가총액은 약 16조원으로 데이터센터 기대감은 아직 충분히 반영되
지 않았으며 최근 주가를 움직이는 요인은 앤트로픽 관련 수급이 더 큰 것
으로 판단. 앤트로픽 상장 시 변동성 확대가 예상되나, 데이터센터 고객과
의 장기계약이 확인되면 수급의 초점이 앤트로픽 대체 투자주에서 AI 인프
라주로 옮겨가며 주가를 다시 견인할 전망. 결국 고객 장기계약 발표와 전
력 규제 개방이 Hyper를 통한 유틸리티 사업 확장 내러티브를 뒷받침하면

Investment Point
▪ 외부 자본으로 짓고 운영으로 버는 AI 팩토리: 6월 NVIDIA와 1GW급 AI
팩토리 공동 구축을 발표. Brookfield가 주도해 최대 90억 달러를 조달하
는 SPV가 GPU·데이터센터 설비를 보유하고, 네이버는 100% 운영 자회
사로 컴퓨팅을 조달해 고객에게 재판매하는 에셋라이트 구조. NVIDIA는
10억 달러 유상증자로 지분 4.5%의 3대 주주. 감가상각·이자를 본체에서
분리해 글로벌 네오클라우드와 달리 초기부터 영업흑자가 가능
▪ 1H27 55MW로 시작해 28년 200MW, 31년 1GW 이상 :  1 단계
200MW는 각 세종·죽전·삼송 등 국내 상면 임차에 말레이시아·일본 리스
를 병행해 확보하고 1Q27부터 매출 인식. 이후 각 세종 증설(설계 최대
270MW), 추가 리스, 신규 그린필드로 2031년 1GW 이상을 목표
▪ IT 1GW 완전 가동 시 네이버 귀속순이익 약 1.1조원 추정: B300 53만장

을 시간당 3달러에 임대하면 매출 19.6조원, SPV 사용료 16.4조원과 운
영비를 차감한 운영사 영업이익 1.16조원(5.9%). SPV 지분 10% 가정
시 지분법이익을 더한 귀속순이익은 1.06조원으로 2025년 지배순이익
(1.95조원)의 절반을 넘는 규모. 임대단가가 시간당 2.8달러를 밑돌면 적
자로 전환해 단가와 SPV 사용료 조건이 핵심 변수
▪ 당면 확인 포인트는 본계약·납입·앵커 고객: Brookfield 12주 독점협상 기
한(10월 중순)이 지나 조건을 막바지 조율 중이며, 본계약으로 SPV의 인
프라 조달이 확정돼야 NVIDIA 납입(10.30)도 최종 확정. 초기 용량에 대
한 수요는 선제 확보했다고 밝혔으나 계약은 미공개로 연내 공개 전망. 사
용료 수준·지급 기간과 네이버의 SPV 소수지분 취득 여부도 미정
▪ 현재 주가는 NVIDIA 신주 발행가 204,500원을 15% 이상 밑돌아 AI 팩

토리 기대가 반영되지 않은 수준. 자사주 1조원 소각으로 증자에 따른 총
주식수 증가는 1.5%에 그침. 결국 앵커 고객 장기계약 공개와 SPV 사용
료 조건 확정이 포털·커머스 플랫폼에서 아시아 AI 인프라 사업자로의 밸
류에이션 리레이팅을 좌우할 전망

기업 개요
▪ Yandex에서 분사해 암스테르담에 본사를 둔 엔비디아 GPU 기반 네오클라
우드 기업. 2Q26 매출 5.82억달러(+454% yoy), ARR 30억달러, RPO
400억달러, EBITDA 마진 41%를 기록했으며, 계약용량 가이던스는 4GW
에서 5GW로 상향
투자 포인트
▪ 선수금 기반의 건강한 B/S: 2Q 체결 계약의 약 70%에 선수금 조건이 포함
되며, 2026년 선수금은 90억달러(캐팩스 가이던스 225억달러의 약 40%)

로 예상. 잔여분은 대부분 전환사채·외부 투자·영업현금흐름으로 충당해, 담
보대출 중심인 경쟁사 대비 금리 민감도가 낮은 재무 구조를 확보
▪ 계약 믹스 전환의 레버리지: 중단기 계약 도입으로 MW당 ACV(연간 계약
가치)는 5년 계약 1,200만달러 대비 중기(1~3년) 최대 2,500만달러, 단기
(~6개월) 최대 4,500만달러로 상승. 조달 부담이 낮아 공격적인 믹스 전환
이 가능하며, 증분 캐파 비중이 높아 2027년부터 실적 레버리지가 본격화
될 전망
▪ 모델 중립성과 Token Factory: 엔비디아 GPU 기반 클러스터로 커스텀 오
픈웨이트 모델까지 효과적으로 서빙. 토큰 사용량 기반 과금으로 수익 구조
를 확장하고, 상각이 끝난 구세대 GPU를 재배치해 자산 수익률을 제고. 대
형 고객사 의존도도 완화 가능
리스크 포인트
▪ 실행력 리스크: 계약이 연말 가동 용량에 집중되어 램프업 지연 시 2027년

실적 눈높이가 하향될 가능성. 단기 계약은 구속력이 약해 매출 지속성 불확

▪ 미국 뉴저지에 본사를 둔 GPU 특화 네오클라우드 기업. 2Q26 매출 25.8
억달러(+112% yoy), EBITDA 마진 59%, OPM 5%를 기록했으며 RPO
는 1,042억달러(+246% yoy) 로 확대. 계약용량  4.2GW, 활성용량
1.5GW이며 연말 활성용량 가이던스는 1.7GW에서 1.85GW로 상향
투자 포인트
▪ 대규모 클러스터 보유가 곧 해자: 전력·부지 등 데이터센터 기초 인프라 병

목으로 가동 중인 클러스터 자체가 진입장벽으로 작용. 활성용량 1.5GW로
네오클라우드 중 최대 규모를 확보해 상대적 가치가 높아지는 구조
▪ GPU 단가 상승: H100·B200 렌탈가는 상승 추세를 유지 중이며 코어위브
의 블랙웰·루빈 가격은 사상 최고치를 경신. 루빈 도입으로 신규 계약 마진
이 5~10%p 개선 중이며, 3Q 매출 가이던스는 35.3억달러(+158% yoy),
4Q OPM은 10%대 초반까지 확대될 전망
▪ Managed Inference ARR 고성장: 오픈웨이트 모델을 토큰 사용량 기반으
로 서빙하며 출시 수개월 만에 ARR 1억달러를 돌파, 연말 2.5억달러 가이
던스를 제시. 구세대 GPU 활용도 제고와 대형 계약 의존도 완화에 기여
리스크 포인트
▪ 자본비용 상승 리스크: 선수금 도입 이전에 빠르게 용량을 확보한 만큼
GPU 담보대출 비중이 높아 이자비용이 매출의 약 25%, 감가상각비가

50%에 달하며 OPM 5%, 순손실 5.67억달러를 기록. 금리 상승이나 렌탈
가 하락 시 수익성이 훼손될 수 있으며, 대형 고객 의존도에 따른 실적 변동

[2027년 경제/외환 전망]
대(大) 차입 경제 VS AI 경제
[경제] 대(大) 차입 경제 VS AI 경제
▪ 2027년 글로벌 경제가 거대한 부채 중심의 차입 경제와 혁신적인 AI 경제가 충돌하는 새로운 국면에 진입할 것으로 전망함
▪ 주요 선진국들은 중물가와 중금리 기조 속에서 안정적인 성장을 꾀할 것으로 예상되지만 급증하는 정부 부채와 하이퍼스케일러의 자금
조달 규모 급증 등이 국채금리 상승으로 이어지면서 신용 리스크를 촉발할 위험이 잠재해 있음. 그러나, AI 투자가 견인하는 높은 명목
성장률이 금리 부담을 상쇄시켜 줄 것으로 예상함. 또한 유가 안정 시 인플레이션 압력이 둔화되면서 미 연준을 위시한 주요 중앙은행의
금리 사이클이 동결 내지 인하 국면으로 진입하면서 국채금리의 안정을 유도할 것으로 기대함
▪ 결국 향후 경제와 금융시장은 차입 비용의 관리와 AI 기술이 선도하는 성장 모멘텀 사이의 선순환 여부에 따라 그 향방이 결정될 것으로

보이며 당사는 긍정적 선순환을 예상함
▪ AI 투자 사이클이 기업의 이익을 주도하며 실질 성장보다 명목 GDP 성장이 중시되는 경제 패러다임의 변화가 예상됨. 동시에 글로벌 경제
패러다임의 변화 역시 AI 사이클을 중심으로 빠르게 진행될 것임. 그 가운데에서도 마이크로가 매크로를 견인하는 현상이 두드러질 것임.
AI발 양극화의 한 단면일 수 있지만 기업이익이 가계소득보다 빠른 증가세를 보이면서 전체 경제를 견인하는 흐름이 강화될 것임
▪ 27년 국내 경제는 26년의 양호한 성장 모멘텀을 이어갈 것으로 예상함. 당사는 26년과 27년 성장률을 각각 3.6%, 3.1% 전망함. 반도체
수출 호조가 27년도에도 국내 경기 사이클을 견인할 것임. 국내 경기 역시 매크로 지표보다 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스와 같은 반도체 기업의
실적 흐름이 경기흐름에 중요한 변수 역할을 할 것임. 즉 ‘기업이익 호조= 높은 명목 GDP 성장률’ 현상이 27년에도 지속될 것으로 전망함

▪ 27년 국내 성장과 관련하여 기대하는 모멘텀은 27년 공공 건설투자 증가임. 27년 국내 메가 프로젝트 본격화가 공공 건설투자 모멘텀
강화로 이어질 것임
▪ 27년 달러 흐름은 제한적 약세를 예상함. 27년 미 연준 금리동결 혹은 금리인하 등으로 주요국간 통화정책 동조화 혹은 역차별화 현상이
달러화 약세 압력으로 작용할 것으로 예상. 즉 미 연준과 주요국 중앙은행간 기준 금리 스프레드 축소 흐름이 지속되면서 달러화는 제한적
약세 흐름을 보일 것임. 이 밖에도 미국과 주요국간 성장률 격차 축소 역시 달러화 약세 요인으로 작용할 것임. 다만 제한적 달러화 약세를
예상하는 이유는 미국 경제가 AI 사이클을 주도하고 있고 미 연준의 기준금리가 여타 주요국에 비해 높은 수준을 유지할 것이기 때문임
▪ 원화는 반도체 호황 지속으로 경상수지 흑자 규모가 27년에도 GDP 대비 20% 내외를 기록할 공산이 크다는 점에서 달러 수급 개선 흐름을

강화시킬 것임. 무엇보다 급격한 경상수지 흑자 폭 확대로 인해 미국의 원화 절상 요구가 강해질 것임

명목 GDP 성장률의 효과는 결국 기업의 이익 사이클에는 긍정적 현상. 대표적으로 2000년대 중반 중국 고정투자 붐 당시 명목 GDP 성장률이 실질
GDP 성장률을 크게 상회한 바 있음

성장률과 실질 GDP성장률간 갭을 주목. 27년에 한국 명목 GDP성장률과 실질 GDP성장률간 갭은 축소되겠지만 과거 평균 수준보다는 높은 수준을

### Page 18

18
[2027년 경제/외환 전망]
대(大) 차입 경제 VS AI 경제
– 국채금리 상승의 구조적 요인과 함께 최근 국채금리 급등의 또 다른 요인, 즉 단기 요인으로는 미국 경제와 금융시장을 사실상 주도하는 트럼프 대통
령, 베센트 재무장관 및 케빈 워시 의장의 정책 혹은 발언의 엇박자 리스크임
– 베센트 장관은 8월초 일본과의 외환시장 공조, 바이백 규모 확대 그리고 ‘트레저리 트위스트(Treasury twist)’ 등을 통해 장기 국채금리 안정을 위한
조치를 실시 중임: 적극적 시장개입을 통한 국채금리 안정 시도
– 케빈 워시 의장은 중앙은행 수장으로서 물가안정을 위해 금리인상 가능성을 강조하는 것이 당연하지만 국채금리 급등 리스크에 대해서는 다소 중립
적 입장을 취하고 있음
▪ 장기 국채금리 안정의 최후 수단 중에 하나인 연준의 국채매입(=양적완화) 가능성을 사실상 차단한 상황에서 국채금리 추가 상승에 대한 미 연준

의 정책 기조는 이전 파월의장과는 다른 기조임 : 적극적 시장 개입보다 중립적 기조 강화
– 트럼프 대통령의 정책 일관성 부족과 조기 금리인하 압박도 국채시장 불안을 확대하는 요인임. 케빈 워시 의장에게 금리 인하를 요구하는 발언을 하
는 동시에 이란에 대한 군사적 공격을 재개한 것은 앞뒤가 맞지 않음 : 트럼프 리스크 가시화 및 미국에 대한 신뢰도 저하에 따른 글로벌 정책 공조 약
화도 미국 국채금리 불안에 큰 리스크임
▪ 더욱이 미국 중간선거에서 공화당이 하원 과반수 의석을 상실할 경우 트럼프 대통령 정책 불확실성 리스크 확대로 장기 국채금리 불안이 확산될
수 있음도 주목
– 결과적으로 디베이스먼트 트레이드 혹은 ABD(Anything But Dollars, 달러를 제외한 모든 것) 투자 심리 확산 가능성이 잠재해 있으며, 이는 국채시
장 변동성 확대와 달러 약세로 이어질 것으로 예상함
정책 엇박자 등으로 국채금리를 안정시킬 대안이 많지 않음

<그림> 22년 9월 트러스 쇼크 당시 영국 10년 국채금리와 파운드화가 요동친 바 있음
자료 : Bloomberg, CEIC, iM증권 리서치본부
– 트러스 쇼크는 2022년 9월 영국 총리직에 오른 트러스 총리가 취임 직후 ‘감세를 통한 경제성장’을 내세우며 70조 원 규모에 육박하는 감세안을 발
표하면서 국채금리 급등으로 발생했던 ‘금리발작’ 충격임
– 일본 다카이치 총리의 확장적 재정정책이 지속되고 있는 가운데 최근에는 인공지능(AI)과 반도체 등을 포함한 17대 핵심 전략 산업에 2040년까지
민관 합동으로 370조엔(약 3,500조원)을 투자하는 대규모 성장 전략 추진 계획을 발표하면서 일본 국채 금리가 추가로 상승하는 부작용이 나타나
고 있음. 이에 따라 일본 정부는 연금투자펀드(GPIF)의 국채 매입 가능성을 언급하는 등 일본 국채시장은 물론 외환시장 불안감이 커지고 있음

<그림> 달러와 미국 국채 금리간 상관관계가 약화됨 <그림> 동반 급등 중인 금 가격과 비트코인 가격
자료 : Bloomberg, CEIC, iM증권 리서치본부 자료 : Bloomberg, CEIC, iM증권 리서치본부
– 미국 국채금리가 장기물을 중심으로 큰 폭 상승했지만 달러화 강세 폭은 제한적이거나 약세 흐름을 유지중임. 미국 국채금리 상승에도 달러화가 약
세 혹은 보합 흐름을 보이는 것은 ‘디베이스먼트 트레이드(법정화폐의 가치 하락(화폐 순도 저하 및 구매력 약화)에 대비해 금 및 가상화폐 같은 실물
·대체자산으로 자금을 옮기는 투자전략)’가 재차 강화되고 있음을 시사
– 디베이스먼트 트레이드 강화 배경: 1) 27년 디스인플레이션 일부 가시화 기대감, 2) 미국 재정 우려 확대에 따른 달러 신뢰도 약화 및 3) 국채금리 안

정을 위한 미국 재무부 혹은 미 연준의 국채 매입 가능성 등임
미국 재정 리스크 부각이 디베이스먼트 트레이드 분위기 강화로 이어질 듯

대(大) 차입 경제 VS AI 경제
<그림> 투자등급(IG)내 하이퍼스케일러의 회사채 발행 비중이 급격히 증가 중 <그림> 27년에도 하이퍼스케일러 회사채 발행규모는 더욱 늘어날 듯
자료 : 골드만삭스, 연합인포맥스, iM증권 리서치본부 자료 : Bloomberg, CEIC, iM증권 리서치본부
– 하이퍼스케일러 회사채 발행이 급증하면서 투자등급(IG) 채권시장의 소화 능력이 한계에 부딪힐 것이라는 경고가 나옴. 26년 기술 업종은 미 달러화
IG 총발행의 20%를 차지하며 사상 최대 비중을 기록 중임. 이런 여파로 미국 달러화 IG 시장에서 기술 업종 회사채의 신용스프레드(가산금리)는 최
근 전체 IG 지수보다 오히려 확대됨. 이는 2010~2025년 대부분 기간 기술 업종 스프레드가 오히려 전체 시장보다 좁게, 즉 더 안전한 채권으로 거
래돼 온 것과는 정반대의 흐름임

– 금융시장이 우려한 것은 "광범위한 부채 발행 물결과 주식 발행 물결이 겹친다면 크레딧과 주식시장 모두에 부정적 신호가 될 것"이라는 점임
대(大) 차입의 시대 : 하이퍼스케일러의 회사채 발행 급증(정부와 함께 자금의 블랙홀)

– 중국 대형 AI기업들의 잇따른 IPO(상장)도 글로벌 자금시장 입장에서 또 다른 부담 요인임. 그동안 중국 AI 기업들이 중국 정부의 보조금을 통해 성
장해 왔지만 중국 정부도 팬데믹 이후 급증한 정부 부채 증가와 소위 그림자 정부 부채의 누적 그리고 저성장 압력으로 AI 기업들에 대한 대규모 지원
이 쉽지 않음. 이에 따라 이전과 달리 중국 대형 AI 기업들은 주식시장 상장을 통해 대규모 자금조달에 나서고 있음
– 한국과 일본 등 주요국 역시 대규모 AI 프로젝트를 진행할 예정이고 이를 위해 대규모 자금이 필요해짐
AI 산업에 올인(All-in) 중인 중국, 대규모 자금조달 창구를 정부에서 민간으로 선회 중

– 한국은행, 26년과 27년 성장률을 각각 3.3%와 2.9%로 대폭 상향 조정함. iM증권은 26년과 27년 성장률을 각각 3.6%, 3.1% 전망
– 한국은행 시나리오별 성장률 전망을 보면 26년과 27년 성장률 전망치의 하향 조정 리스크와 상향 조정 리스크를 언급함. 이중 반도체 사이클과 관
련하여 낙관적 시나리오가 전개될 경우 26년과 27년 성장률은 각각 +0.2%p와 +0.6%p 상향 조정될 수 있을 것으로 전망함. 반도체 경기의 낙관적
시나리오를 전제할 경우 26년과 27년 성장률 모두 3.5%가 된다는 것으로 27년 성장률이 26년보다 둔화될 것이라는 기본 전망을 뒤집을 수 있는

▶ Economist 최규호 choi.gh@hanwha.com 02-3772-7720

8 월 광공업 생산 전월대비 4.8% 감소

자료: 국가데이터처, 한화투자증권 리서치센터

반도체 수출은 여전히 견조

자료: 관세청, 산업통상부, 한화투자증권 리서치센터

[ Compliance Notice ] 
이 자료는 투자자의 증권투자를 돕기 위해 당사 고객에 한하여 배
포되는 자료로서 저작권이 당사에 있으며 불법 복제 및 배포를 금
합니다. 이 자료에 수록된 내용은 당사 리서치센터가 신뢰할 만한 
자료나 정보출처로부터 얻은 것이지만, 당사는 그 정확성이나 완
전성을 보장할 수 없습니다. 따라서 이 자료는 어떠한 경우에도 고
객의 증권투자 결과와 관련된 법적 책임소재에 대한 증빙으로 사
용될 수 없습니다. 
 향후 국내 성장은 제조업이 주도할 전망입니다. 금번 지표 부진은 주로 
일시적인 요인들의 영향입니다. 견조한 반도체 수출과 정부의 제조업 
지원 정책을 고려하면, 수출과 투자 환경은 양호할 것이라 기대합니다. 
생산과 소비, 투자 동반 감소 
생산: 광공업 생산은 전월대비 4.8% 감소. 반도체(-2.2%) 생산이 감소 
전환했고, 자동차(-24.8%) 생산이 2020년 2월 이후 가장 크게 줄었음. 
고무·플라스틱(-11.0%)과 의약품(-8.8%) 생산 또한 감소. 다만 서비
스업(+0.5%) 생산 증가로 전산업 생산은 전월대비 1.3% 감소에 그침 
소비: 소매판매는 전월대비 1.8% 감소. 승용차 등을 중심으로 내구재
(-4.5%) 판매가 재차 줄었고, 비내구재(-1.6%) 판매도 감소. 대형마트
(-5.9%)와 면세점(-11.5%) 판매 감소 전환 
투자: 설비투자는 전월대비 9.5% 감소. 기계류(+1.6%) 투자가 4개월 
연속 늘었지만, 운송장비(-32.8%) 투자가 1997년 1월 이후 가장 크게 
감소했기 때문. 전기 및 전자기기 투자도 전월대비 2.7% 감소 
제조업 부담은 일시적, 전망은 양호 
제조업 주도 성장 지속 전망. 반도체 업황이 여전히 양호하고, 국내 투
자 환경 또한 개선되고 있음 
수출과 투자는 지속적으로 성장에 기여할 것. 금번 광공업 생산 부진은 
조업일수 감소와 현대차 파업 여파에 따른 자동차, 고무·플라스틱 업황 
타격을 감안할 필요. 반도체 수출과 교역조건이 여전히 양호한 가운데, 
제조업 출하-재고 사이클도 자동차 업종을 제외하면 대체로 개선됐음. 
설비투자 또한 정부의 반도체 특별법, 남부권 반도체 혁신 벨트 추진 
등을 고려하면 반도체 중심으로 늘어날 것 
내수가 큰 부담이 되지는 않을 전망. 소매판매 감소가 이어지고 있지만 
소비심리는 양호한 수준을 유지. 산업통상부가 발표한 주요 유통업체 
매출도 증가세(8월 +7.7% YoY)를 이어가고 있음. 소비자물가 부담도 
점진적으로 완화될 가능성이 높아 실질구매력 부담도 크지 않음. 내수 
우려가 강하지 않다면, 제조업 주도 하에 연간 3%대 성장 유력

AI Jitters Continue While Fed Pauses Hiking Rates

YARDENI QUICKTAKES
AI Jitters Continue While Fed
Pauses Hiking Rates
By Ed Yardeni & Elias Griepentrog • 29 Oct 2026
View in browser

I. The AI Boom Versus The AI Trade
AI jitters will be back tomorrow after taking a breather so far this week, as
encouraging developments surrounding the AI investment boom helped
restore confidence and lift technology stocks. The S&P 500 rose 0.3% on
Wednesday, moving back above its 50-day moving average (chart).

### Page 2

The Nasdaq-100 advanced 0.6%, recovering toward its 50-day moving
average while remaining above its 200-day moving average (chart).
Among chipmakers, Micron jumped 5.9%, AMD gained 3.2%, and
Broadcom rose 2.8% (chart). SK Hynix shares surged as much as 9.4% in
Seoul following blockbuster earnings.
Three recent developments helped revive confidence in the AI trade:
(1) More spending. $235 billion in prospective AI financing emerged this
week, including Anthropic's expected $100 billion IPO raise, Meta's plans

to raise up to $95 billion through equity issuance, and SpaceX's $40 billion
debt deal to purchase GPUs. These developments suggest capital
remains available for the AI buildout, with equity markets providing an
alternative if debt financing tightens.

### Page 3

(2) Encouraging AI economics. Anthropic's S-1 filing offered five
encouraging signals about the sustainability of compute demand. First, H1
revenues surged from $1.2 billion to $16.3 billion y/y. Second, operating
losses narrowed from $2.1 billion to $693 million, with Q2 marking its first
quarterly operating profit. Third, 11,900 customers now spend at least
$100,000 annually, up from roughly 950 a year earlier. Fourth, revenue
per dollar of compute expense increased more than fivefold to $2.08.

Fifth, Anthropic held $131.7 billion in cash and short-term investments to
finance expansion.
(3) Strong semiconductor earnings. SK Hynix's Q3 results reinforced
confidence in AI infrastructure demand. Operating profit surged more than
sevenfold y/y, while the company announced roughly $75 billion in
shareholder returns. Most encouragingly, management expects memory
shortages through 2030, with production effectively sold out through 2029,
suggesting durable demand and pricing power.

These developments reinforce our view that the AI investment boom is
here to stay. But that doesn't mean that the AI trade won't remain jittery.
This evening, Alphabet shares are down about 10% after the company
missed Q3 consensus revenues and earnings estimates. Free cash flow
was also more negative than expected, while the company remains
committed to significant capex of over $200 billion this year and $300
billion in 2027. Long-term debt rose to $125.1 billion, up from $21.6 billion

a year earlier.
There was some good news. Cloud revenue more than doubled to $30.7
billion. Google said its Gemini app reached 1 billion users, making it the
fastest-growing product in its history. Furthermore, Microsoft shares rose
4% in extended trading this evening after the company reported better-
than-expected quarterly results, driven by 48% growth in its Azure cloud
infrastructure business.
II. The Fed Pauses Before Midterm Elections
The FOMC voted 10-2 Wednesday to hold the federal funds rate at

3.75%-4.00%, with Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack favoring a 25bps hike.
Chair Kevin Warsh acknowledged robust economic growth, a healthy
labor market, stubborn inflation, and financial conditions that aren't tight.
Yet he cited tightening financial conditions, anchored inflation

### Page 4

expectations, and improving productivity as reasons for patience. Here's
more:
(1) Economic activity. Warsh observed that "economic growth has
strengthened." Consumer spending remains robust and business
investment is growing at a double-digit pace. The capex story, he said, is
"not just robust, not just strong, but it is broadening."
(2) Labor market. Unemployment is lower than a year ago, payroll growth
has improved, and initial jobless claims remain near historic lows.

Employment conditions are "quite positive," Warsh said, with FOMC
discussions focused primarily on price stability.
(3) Inflation. "Inflation is too high," Warsh acknowledged, warning that
rising energy prices could spread through the economy. He rejected a
higher implicit inflation target: "There's no soft inflation target, there's no
implicit inflation target." Still, he believes inflation expectations remain
anchored.
(4) Financial conditions. Warsh noted that tighter financial conditions are

prompting more selective capital allocation. Rejecting claims that AI
investment is insensitive to interest rates, he observed that "interest rates
get in the cracks" as credit spreads have widened for some borrowers.
Nevertheless, "while overall financial conditions are tighter, I'm unwilling
and unable to call them tight."
(5) Productivity. Warsh disputed that robust growth necessarily implies
overheating: "That isn't the judgment of most of my colleagues." Improving

productivity, much of it predating recent AI advances, may have raised
potential growth without fueling inflation.
(6) Revamping the Fed. Warsh reiterated his opposition to forward
guidance outside crises. Yet other officials' comments shifted market
expectations away from an October hike despite hotter-than-expected
September CPI and PPI inflation reports, suggesting forward guidance
remains intact. He also plans to dedicate one FOMC meeting in 2027 and

two in 2028 to monetary policy strategy.
In our view, stronger productivity growth will let the economy expand
faster without adding inflationary pressure. That could be an argument

### Page 5

against restrictive monetary policy, but not against returning to neutral,
which we estimate at 4.25%-4.50%. We agree that September's hike
“removed a dose of accommodation,” but believe another 50bps is
needed to remove the rest. The Fed doesn't need to throw sand in the
economy's gears. It just needs to take its foot off the accelerator. We
wouldn't rule out a 50bps hike in December.

 Do không còn h ạch toán FPT Telecom (FOX) là công ty con, d oanh thu 2Q2026 của 
FPT giảm mạnh còn 13,810 tỷ VND (-17% YoY). Lợi nhuận sau thuế công ty mẹ không 
bị ảnh hưởng bởi thay đổi hạch toán đạt 2,568 tỷ VND (14% YoY). Mảng dịch vụ CNTT 
tại thị trường nước ngoài tiếp tục là đ ộng lực tăng trư ởng chính, đạt doanh thu và 
LNTT lần lượt là 9,868/1,538 tỷ VND (16.3% /19.3% YoY).

Sự chuyển dịch chi tiêu từ dịch vụ IT truyền thống sang chuyển đổi số và tích hợp AI 
được kỳ vọng sẽ diễn ra ngày m ột mạnh mẽ khi: i) Sự phát triển của năng l ực tính 
toán giúp kéo giảm chi phí token (đơn v ị năng lực tính toán của AI) và thúc đ ẩy nhu 
cầu sử dụng AI của doanh nghiệp; ii) Các mô hình AI mã nguồn mở gia tăng lựa chọn 
cho người dùng sẽ thúc đẩy chi tiêu

Đối với các doanh nghiệp ứng dụng sâu các mô hình AI phục vụ hoạt động kinh doanh 
như FPT , chúng tôi nhận thấy xu hướng tối ưu chi phí tốt hơn nhờ khả năng sử dụng 
các mô hình AI đ ến từ đa dạng nhà cung c ấp; với chi phí trên hi ệu năng tính toán 
được cải thi ện. Trong k ịch b ản cơ s ở, chúng tôi d ự báo biên l ợi nhuận trước thu ế 
mảng CNTT nước ngoài sẽ ổn định ở mức 15.4% nhờ duy trì chi ến lược quản trị chi 
phí hiệu quả qua đó giúp LNTT 2026/2027 đạt 6,198/7,087 tỷ VND (13.3%/14.3% YoY).

Dựa trên định giá FCFF và P/E, triển vọng kinh doanh cũng như xem xét các rủi ro có 
thể phát sinh, chúng tôi khuyến nghị MUA đối với cổ phiếu FPT . Giá mục tiêu là 86,000 
VND/cổ phiếu.

Doanh thu Quý 2/2026 giảm nhẹ, đạt 2,432 tỷ VND (-3% YoY/-2% QoQ), trong khi l ợi 
nhuận sau thuế công ty mẹ đạt 632 tỷ VND (+1% YoY/-11.5% QoQ), do doanh thu của 
mảng bất động sản suy giảm. Qua đó, REE hoàn thành lần lượt 40%/47.8% kế hoạch 
doanh thu và LNST công ty mẹ 2026.

Trong Q2.2026, tổng sản lượng phát đi ện của REE tăng nh ẹ, đạt 2.8 tỷ kWh (+2.3% 
YoY) với đóng góp tăng trưởng rõ nét đến từ mảng điện gió khi dự án Duyên Hải V1-4 
bắt đầu vận hành; tuy nhiên  sản lượng thủy điện suy gi ảm do tác đ ộng tiêu c ực từ 
pha thời tiết El Nino, đạt 1.1 tỷ kWh.

Với năng lực chuyên môn được nâng cao, mảng M&E ghi nhận những dấu hiệu phục 
hồi tích cực trong giá trị hợp đồng ký mới trong 1H.2026, 5,865 tỷ VND (cao hơn 53.9% 
so với giá trị ký mới cả năm 2025). KBSV dự phóng doanh thu c ủa mảng M&E sẽ đạt 
4,499/5,190 tỷ VND (+28%/15% YoY) trong 2026/2027.

Hội tụ bởi 3 yếu tố: i) Định hướng phát triển kinh tế Hồ Chí Minh trở thành trung tâm 
tài chính quốc tế; ii) Hạ tầng giao thông ngày một được hoàn thiện và iii) Chi phí thuê 
cạnh tranh so với chất lượng dịch vụ của E. Town 6, KBSV dự phóng doanh thu mảng 
cho thuê văn phòng trong 2026/2027 tăng trưởng +14%/6.2% YoY.

Dựa trên đ ịnh giá SOTP , triển vọng kinh doanh cũng như xem xét các r ủi ro có th ể 
phát sinh, chúng tôi khuy ến nghị MUA đối với cổ phiếu REE. Giá m ục tiêu là 58,100 
VND/cổ phiếu, cao hơn 28.3% so với mức giá đóng cửa tại ngày 15/09/2026.

 Trong Quý 2/2026, POW ghi nhận Doanh thu và LNST cổ đông công ty mẹ đạt lần lượt 
20,308 tỷ VND (116.1% YoY) và 3,519 tỷ VND (484.6% YoY) chủ yếu nhờ các khoản thu 
nhập từ chênh lệch tiền khí của nhiệt điện Cà Mau và tỷ giá của nhiệt điện Vũng Áng.

nhuận sau thuế công ty mẹ.

Chúng tôi cho r ằng nhà máy nhi ệt than Vũng Áng trong 2026 s ẽ được duy trì công 
suất huy động ở mức cao nhờ: i) Xác suất diễn ra El Nino tăng cao và dự kiến kéo dài 
đến đầu 2027, ii) Nguồn cung than trong nước được bảo đảm từ các đối tác (TKV, TCT 
Đông B ắc) và d ự trữ than d ồi dào c ủa doanh nghi ệp ghi nh ận ở mức cao trong 
Q2/2026.

Dự án đường dây 500kV Mạch 3 đi vào vận hành giúp giảm áp lực cạnh tranh của các 
nhà máy điện tại khu vực phía Nam, qua đó kỳ vọng doanh thu của NT1&2 trong năm 
2026 đạt 11,104 tỷ VND (5.3% YoY). Đối với dự án điện NT3&4, khoản thu nhập chênh 
lệch sản lượng theo giá công suất do sản lượng điện thực tế thấp hơn so với tỷ lệ Qc 
65% của nhà máy được duy trì sang 2H26 và 2027 sẽ giúp cho dự án ghi nhận doanh 
thu lần lượt 17,848/17,621 tỷ VND doanh thu trong 2026/2027.

Dựa trên định giá SOTP và EV/EBITDA, tri ển vọng kinh doanh cũng như xem xét các 
rủi ro có th ể phát sinh, chúng tôi khuy ến nghị MUA đối với cổ phiếu POW. Giá m ục 
tiêu là 18,100 VND/cổ phiếu.

không thúc đ ẩy doanh thu t ại các

Mở rộng mạng lưới tạo động lực tăng

Cơ c ấu kinh doanh và hi ệu qu ả vận

Chúng tôi khuyến nghị MUA, giá mục

2Q2026, AST ghi nh ận doanh thu và LNST đ ạt 479/92 t ỷ VND (+22%/19% yoy), với 
động lực chủ yếu đến từ (1) đóng góp từ 19 điểm kinh doanh mở mới tại T3 Tân Sơn 
Nhất và (2) tăng trưởng tích cực của các mảng hàng miễn thuế, nhà hàng - fastfood 
và phòng ch ờ thương gia. Lũy k ế 6T2026, doanh thu và LNST đ ạt 1,035/221 t ỷ VND 
(+33%/46% yoy), lần lượt hoàn thành 48%/49% kế hoạch năm.

Chúng tôi dự phóng lượng khách quốc tế/nội địa tại các thị trường AST khai thác tăng 
bình quân 11%/5% mỗi năm đến 2030. Lưu lượng và tỷ trọng khách quốc tế gia tăng 
được kỳ vọng thúc đẩy số giao dịch và doanh thu bình quân trên mỗi khách, đặc biệt 
tại mảng miễn thuế, bán lẻ và phòng chờ.

Chúng tôi dự phóng số điểm kinh doanh AST tăng từ 145 điểm cuối năm 2026 lên 182 
điểm năm 2030. Sau đóng góp t ừ 19 điểm tại T3 Tân Sơn Nh ất và 6 điểm mới tại T2 
Nội Bài từ 2025 - 2026, các dự án Long Thành, Phú Qu ốc và Gia Bình ti ếp tục mở ra 
dư địa mở rộng mạng lưới trong trung và dài hạn cho doanh nghiệp.

Việc mở rộng các hoạt động mang lại lợi nhuận cao, bao gồm hàng miễn thuế, phòng 
chờ thương gia và tối ưu hoạt động tại các điểm kinh doanh đ ược kỳ vọng tác động 
tích c ực lên biên l ợi nhu ận của AST . Chúng tôi dự phóng biên l ợi nhu ận g ộp đ ạt 
64.7%/65.5% trong năm 2026/2027, hỗ trợ LNST công ty mẹ tăng lần lượt 48%/17% 
yoy.

Chúng tôi khuy ến nghị MUA đối với AST , giá mục tiêu 76 ,500 VND/cổ phiếu, tương 
đương tiềm năng tăng giá 20% so với giá đóng cửa ngày 21/09/2026.

thúc đẩy nhờ thời tiết nắng nóng hơn; 
trong khi tri ển v ọng nhóm khách 
hàng công nghi ệp b ị ảnh hư ởng b ởi 
bất lợi thuế quan

Đơn giá thu gom, vận chuyện và xử 
lý rác thải được phê duyệt cho phép 
cải thiện doanh thu và lợi nhuận của 
mảng này

Khuyến nghị MUA với giá mục tiêu 
59,000 VNĐ/cổ phiếu

Doanh thu 2Q2026 đạt 1,222 tỷ (-8% YoY/18.1% QoQ) và LNST công ty mẹ đạt 325 tỷ 
VND (7% YoY/55% QoQ), ghi nhận tăng trưởng của tất cả các mảng. Mảng cung cấp 
nước tăng trưởng ổn định, tiếp tục là trụ cột chính của BWE, đóng góp doanh thu 785 
tỷ VND (+12% YoY/12% QoQ) nhờ nhà máy nước Long An v ận hành từ Q3/2025 giúp 
sản lượng nước tăng 28% YoY.

Cường độ và thời gian kéo dài c ủa các đ ợt nắng nóng trong 2026/2027 là cơ s ở để 
chúng tôi đi ều chỉnh tăng tăng trư ởng tiêu th ụ nước của nhóm khách hàng dân cư 
tại Bình Dương và Bình Phư ớc trong năm 2026 - 2027 lên mức 7.5/6.5% YoY. Trái lại, 
triển vọng tăng trưởng tiêu thụ nước nhóm sản xuất ảm đạm do tình hình thuế quan 
có diễn biến bất lợi trong ngắn hạn cho các ngành xu ất khẩu truyền thống của Việt 
Nam.

UBND TP .HCM công bố đơn giá thu gom, vận chuyển và xử lý rác thải mới, tăng mạnh 
từ 50-150% nhằm phản ánh đầy đủ và chính xác hơn các chi phí phát sinh trong thực 
tế. Chúng tôi cho rằng điều này sẽ tác động tích cực với BWE khi các dự án của doanh 
nghiệp ở mảng này s ẽ vận hành hi ệu quả hơn. Dự báo doanh thu và l ợi nhuận gộp 
của mảng xử lý rác thải lần lượt đạt 1,069/1,234 và 165.7/180.7 tỷ VND lần lượt trong 
2026/2027, tương ứng mức tăng 34%/15% và 27%/9% YoY.

Kết hợp 2 phương pháp định giá FCFF và EV/EBITDA, KBSV khuyến nghị MUA với BWE, 
giá mục tiêu 59,000 VND, tương đương với mức lợi suất kỳ vọng 42.2% so với giá đóng 
cửa ngày 22/09/2026.

Ngưỡng kỹ thuật

VNINDEX điều chỉnh trở lại trong tuần qua sau khi gặp thử thách tại vùng cản quanh 1850, 
hình thành cây nến tuần giảm điểm nhưng với phần bóng dưới khá dài cho thấy sự tham 
gia tích cực của lực cầu bắt đáy tại vùng hỗ trợ gần. Trên khung ngày, nhịp giảm mạnh giữa 
tuần đã khiến chỉ số đánh mất đáy ngắn hạn tuần trước và chớm cắt xuống dưới SMA200, 
trong khi phiên hồi phục cuối tuần chưa cho thấy sự cải thiện rõ rệt của lực cầu. Mặc dù 
diễn biến này cho thấy áp lực điều chỉnh vẫn có thể còn tiếp diễn, tuy nhiên khi xu hướng 
tăng ngắn hạn chưa bị phá vỡ, VNINDEX được kỳ vọng sẽ nhận được lực đỡ tại vùng hỗ trợ 
gần quanh 1750, tương ứng vùng hợp lưu quanh SMA50, và có cơ hội hồi phục trở lại.

Danh mục đầu tư mẫu

Phương pháp tiếp cận: 
- Danh mục tập hợp các cổ phiếu tiềm năng nhất được KBSV 
lựa chọn và tái cơ cấu theo tháng. 
- Ngưỡng cắt lỗ cần được cân nhắc cho mỗi mã là -15%. 
- Danh mục giả định luôn duy trì tỷ trọng 100% là cổ phiếu với 
trọng số được phân bổ đều giữa các mã.

Lưu ý:  
- NĐT được khuyến nghị mua tại mức giá bằng hoặc thấp hơn 
giá khuyến nghị mua. 
- Lợi nhuận kỳ vọng được tính theo giá khuyến nghị mua. 
 So sánh hiệu suất với VN30 Index

Danh mục đầu tư mẫu 
Mã Giá đóng cửa tuần Biến động từ đầu tháng Giá khuyến nghị mua Giá mục tiêu Lợi nhuận kỳ vọng Điểm nhấn đầu tư Báo cáo phân tích 
FRT 141.90 -2.7% 124.30 143.00 15.0% 
- Sau khi phủ sóng các thành phố lớn, chuỗi Long Châu đang mở rộng sang các vùng cấp 2, 3.

#rbnz #newzealand
First Impressions: RBNZ Monetary Policy Review October 2026
By Kelly Eckhold & Westpac New Zealand Economics
12:30 October 28 2026 Share
The RBNZ left the OCR unchanged at 2.75% (in contrast to market expectation for a hike,
including ourselves).
The MPC has stuck to its strategy of pausing to assess the impact of tightening already done. There is
a clear split among the MPC members on where the risks lie although it seems clear enough that

higher interest rates are in the future the data evolves as the Committee expects. Key factors to focus
on are data on inflation expectations, the global economy (and potential downside risks there) and the

### Page 2

path of fuel prices.  We expect a 25 bp increase in the OCR in December to 3% and are reverting to
the OCR profile we had up until mid last week.  We don't think the December hike is a done deal as the
data will inform the next move. We will revert with more detail after the press conference. 
Key takeouts from the minutes below.

Media contact
Kelly Eckhold
Chief economist 
+64 9 348 9382
+64 21 786 758
Key takeouts
Category 2 September 2026 meeting 28 October 2026 meeting
The next policy
decision
Future policy decisions will depend
on the Committee’s judgement of the
balance of risks to medium-term
inflation.
Members discussed that information
arriving over the next six weeks
could meaningfully change the
appropriate policy stance in either
direction.
  Conditional on the central economic
outlook, members judged that the
OCR may need to increase further.
All members agreed that tighter
monetary policy is likely to be
required, but remains conditional on
the economic outlook.
  However, the future OCR path is not
pre-determined.

The medium term
direction for the
OCR
The Committee judges that gradually
removing monetary stimulus is
appropriate to return inflation to the
2 percent target mid-point while
supporting growth and employment.
Further OCR increases likely, but
are conditional on the outlook

### Page 3

Category 2 September 2026 meeting 28 October 2026 meeting
  All members agreed that gradually
removing monetary stimulus is
consistent with achieving the
medium-term inflation target,
conditional on the outlook.
If domestic pricing pressures fail to
moderate sufficiently or broaden
beyond what costs and normal pass-
through can explain, this could
warrant further tightening.
  Conditional on the central economic
outlook, members judged that the
OCR may need to increase further.
On the other hand, subdued pricing
pressures could require holding at
future meetings.
    And if the global economy turns
sharply down, materially weakening
demand and the inflation outlook,
this could alter the desired stance,
including leading to monetary
easing.

The neutral OCR   The Committee acknowledged that
the neutral interest rate has a wide
range of plausible estimates.
    Members noted that the increase in
global long-term yields may partly
signal a higher global neutral
interest rate, due to higher inflation
expectations, war destruction and
demand for capital to support AI
investment.
    Higher global interest rates could
bring forward a potential global
downturn, and the neutral interest
rate could decline rapidly in the
event of an abrupt global
adjustment.

### Page 4

Category 2 September 2026 meeting 28 October 2026 meeting

The strength of
economic activity
After lacklustre growth in the June
quarter, New Zealand's economic
recovery has most likely resumed
but remains uneven.
The New Zealand economy
continues to recover, although
conditions remain uneven.
  The recovery is expected to
strengthen and broaden.
The Committee noted that GDP
growth was more than expected
through the first half of 2026.
  The Committee assessed that
growth was lacklustre in the second
quarter of 2026.
Business survey measures point to
continued expansion in economic
activity.
  The economic recovery is expected
to have resumed in the third quarter,
while remaining uneven across
sectors and regions.
Household consumption has been
weak and the aggregate saving rate
is estimated to be 3.7 percent,
above the 10-year average of 1
percent.

The global
economic
outlook
The global economy is facing
significant risks that could affect
commodity prices and demand for
exports.
Global growth has been resilient but
is increasingly fragile given
geopolitical tensions, high energy
prices, financial stresses, and
surging AI-related investment.
  Despite recent geopolitical events,
economic growth in New Zealand’s
trading partners has remained
resilient and the outlook has
improved.
The Committee assessed that there
are significant risks to the global
economic outlook.

### Page 5

Category 2 September 2026 meeting 28 October 2026 meeting
  Although risks to the global economy
remain heightened, the Committee
expects global economic conditions
to remain favourable for New
Zealand’s export facing businesses
over the medium term.
The Committee noted that a global
downturn could occur abruptly.

The labour
market
Conditions in the labour market
should improve as the recovery
gathers pace.
Employment growth remains
subdued and higher prices will
further reduce real incomes and
purchasing power.
  Employment growth has not been
sufficient to fully absorb new
entrants into the labour market and
unemployment is elevated,
particularly in Auckland and
Wellington and for youth and the
long-term unemployed.
Employment intentions remain
weak, pointing to continued slow
recovery in the labour market.
  The labour market is expected to
slowly improve, with employment
growing and unemployment falling
as the economy recovers.
To date, wage growth has been
subdued, and medium-term inflation
expectations have remained stable.
  On balance, the Committee
assesses that spare capacity
remains in the economy, particularly
in the labour market.

### Page 6

Category 2 September 2026 meeting 28 October 2026 meeting
The short term
inflation outlook
Inflation increased to 4.1 percent in
the June quarter because of higher
fuel prices arising from the conflict in
the Middle East.
Annual inflation is expected to
increase to 4.4 percent in the
December quarter, largely reflecting
current futures prices for fuel.
  The Committee expects inflation to
remain elevated this year before
returning to the target band by mid-
2027 and reaching the 2 percent
mid-point later next year.
Near-term inflation forecasts are
uncertain given volatility in prices for
oil and refined fuels.
    Direct effects of higher fuel prices
will drop out of the annual inflation
calculation in late 2027 if prices for
refined petroleum products stabilise
or fall.

The medium term
inflation outlook
Core inflation, expected wage
growth, and inflation expectations
remain consistent with inflation
returning to the 1 to 3 percent target
band by mid-2027 and the 2 percent
target midpoint later next year.
The Committee is focused on
returning inflation to the 2 percent
target mid-point over the medium
term, discounting temporary
disturbances to inflation and
avoiding unnecessary economic
instability.
  Longer-term inflation expectations
remain near 2 percent, while most
measures of one and two-year-
ahead inflation expectations have
fallen since May.
Impacts on shortterm pricing
behaviour appear to have been
contained and medium-term inflation
expectations remain well anchored.
  Currently, indicators of medium-term
inflation are consistent with inflation
returning to target.
But the longer inflation remains high,
the greater the risk of higher costs
feeding into inflation expectations
and price- and wage-setting
behaviour, making inflation more
persistent.

### Page 7

Category 2 September 2026 meeting 28 October 2026 meeting

The balance of
risks for
economic growth
and inflation
New Zealand’s economic recovery
could be stronger or weaker than
expected and price pressures could
generate more persistent inflation.
New Zealand’s recovery could be
stronger than expected but could
also lose momentum if the global
environment deteriorates or export
strength does not flow through to
jobs, incomes and household
spending.
  Consumption growth could be
subdued if employment and house
price growth remain weak, or if
precautionary behaviour persists.
There is a risk that inflation becomes
entrenched before conventional
expectations measures respond,
despite the previous two OCR
increases.
  Alternatively, consumption growth
could be stronger and absorb spare
capacity faster than currently
anticipated.
In addition, the world economy could
tip abruptly into a downturn causing
weaker inflation over the medium
term.
  All members agreed that downside
risks to activity were significant and
that the recovery could remain
uneven.
It is also possible that geopolitical
escalation could drive fuel prices
higher while weakening global
economic activity at the same time.

Key arguments
advanced by
more hawkish
MPC members
Hayley Gourley, Karen Silk,
Prasanna Gai and Anna Breman
saw upside risks to inflation relative
to the central projection.
Hayley Gourley, Paul Conway and
Karen Silk favoured increasing the
OCR by 25 basis points at this
meeting.

### Page 8

Category 2 September 2026 meeting 28 October 2026 meeting
  These members observed that more
persistence in energy and
petrochemical prices could raise
near-term inflation risks, impact
price-setting behaviour, and lead to
more sticky inflation over the
medium term.
These members emphasised that
core inflation has been above levels
consistent with headline inflation at
the target mid-point for some time.
  Price-setting can be a front-loaded
process, meaning businesses could
raise domestic prices more than
import costs warrant.
This increases the risk of inflation
becoming entrenched in price-
setting behaviour as the conflict and
its consequences endure, including
through higher freight and shipping
costs.
  These factors increase the risk that
monetary policy needs to lean
against broader inflation pressures.
Acting now would guard against
sustained inflation pressures and
potentially reduce the risk of needing
to do more with interest rates later.

Key arguments
advanced by
more dovish MPC
members in each
meeting
Paul Conway and Carl Hansen saw
risks to inflation as balanced.
Anna Breman, Carl Hansen,
Rebecca Williams and Prasanna Gai
favoured holding the OCR at this
meeting as two recent OCR
increases allow the Committee to
take further time to assess their
effects and economic developments.
  These members shared concerns
that high inflation could become
embedded through price-setting
behaviour.
Actual inflation was lower than
expected, reflecting smaller indirect
effects of higher fuels prices, and
medium-term inflation expectations
and wage growth remain consistent
with returning inflation to the target
mid-point.

Cost shock hit proﬁtability, but for some
airlines more than others

Jet fuel is often the largest or second-largest cost item for airlines.
In 2025, it accounted for 27% of total operational costs on average.
This share could move towards 35% in 2026 as a result of
persistently high jet fuel prices and elevated crack spreads, caused
by the loss of Middle Eastern supplies and tight global availability.
Further geopolitical developments remain highly uncertain. Even if
the Middle East conﬂict is resolved and oil prices retreat, tight

reﬁnery capacity and depleted inventories are likely to keep middle-
distillate prices, including jet fuel, elevated well into 2027.
High fuel prices impact proﬁts in US and
Europe, low cost carriers most vulnerable

Source: Company reports, ING Research
Fuel hedging provides less cushioning in
2027; fares must respond
Airlines employ very diﬀerent strategies to protect themselves
against fuel price shocks, using derivatives based on crude oil or jet
fuel. European airlines generally hedged 40-90% of their jet fuel
consumption, cushioning the initial impact of the price shock.
However, the Middle East conﬂict has lasted too long to avoid a

signiﬁcant impact. Existing hedges gradually roll oﬀ, increasing
exposure to prevailing market prices. Ryanair, which remains (80%)
hedged until the second quarter of 2027, has already warned of
signiﬁcantly higher fares.
Outside, the picture is mixed, but hedge ratios are generally lower,
and airlines in the US and China, for instance, don’t hedge at all.
This means that two airlines operating similar routes can face very
diﬀerent fuel bills.
Airline tickets in the US responded much

faster to the cost shock than in Europe

Fares already sharply higher in the US, less
so in Europe
The fuel price shock will increasingly feed through into higher fares.
US airlines’ practice of retaining relatively high exposure to fuel price
volatility resulted in an almost immediate pass-through, with ticket
prices rising solidly in the months after jet fuel prices started to rise.

It is also easier to raise prices when domestic competitors face a
similar cost shock.
The situation is diﬀerent in Europe, where hedging provided more
initial protection. This also means fares may still need to rise
signiﬁcantly if fuel prices fail to fall. Coverage gradually expires as
2027 progresses, leaving airlines increasingly exposed to higher
spot prices.
Airline proﬁts hit, but industry remains
proﬁtable

### Page 9

Source: IATA, *ING Research based on IATA
More factors are driving up costs,
particularly in Europe
Jet fuel is the clear outlier this year, but wage and maintenance
costs are also rising faster than the average price level. Borrowing
costs and aircraft leasing rates remain another factor, although the
impact depends on individual airlines’ strategies and ﬁnancial
structures.
European airlines also face rising costs from the European Union
Emissions Trading System (ETS) for ﬂights within the European

Economic Area. In addition, fuel suppliers are required to blend
sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) under ReFuelEU Aviation, starting at
2% and rising to 6% by 2030*. SAF still trades at a signiﬁcant
premium. This puts a price on emissions, and in combination, this
adds some $300 per tonne of jet fuel in 2026 (BNEF, ING Research).
Meanwhile, France and the Netherlands have either raised or plan
to raise ticket taxes, particularly on long-haul ﬂying, while Germany

has scaled its levy back and Sweden has abolished it.
High fuel prices put more pressure on low-
cost carriers
*A revision proposal is in progress for aviation, drawing a circle of 5,000 km around
Frankfurt for application of ETS, which would hit Middle East airlines most as they will
then be in scope. **In 2025, the blend rate stood at 2.8%

### Page 10

Low-cost carriers are particularly exposed because fuel accounts
for a larger share of their cost base, and proﬁt bases are more
vulnerable. High hedge ratios initially cushion volatility, but these
hedges gradually roll oﬀ. The more challenging environment is
already visible in the performance of several European low-cost
carriers and will remain an important theme in 2027 if fuel prices
stay elevated.
Premium carriers have more room to manoeuvre. Demand for

premium seats (business, premium economy) is less price-
sensitive, providing airlines with greater scope to pass on higher
costs. Both United Airlines and Delta Airlines reported little impact
after price increases of 15-20% in the second to third quarters.
Passengers are booking later, but airlines continue to indicate a
strong propensity to ﬂy, especially in premium and premium-
economy classes. A minority also accounts for a large share of
ﬂights. In the Netherlands, for example, 25% of people account for

75% of journeys. These frequent travellers tend to be less price-
sensitive.
There has therefore been some demand destruction wiping out part
of the underlying growth. So far, though, the propensity to travel
has remained resilient.
Aviation remains proﬁtable, but margins hit
a post-pandemic low
The fuel shock has signiﬁcantly aﬀected margins. On average,
proﬁts in the global industry are expected to drop meaningfully
below 5%. Airlines including Ryanair, Southwest Airlines and AirAsia

have scaled back capacity on unproﬁtable routes as elevated fuel
prices persisted longer than expected.
According to global aviation consultancy Cirium, around 1% of
global air travel capacity will be removed heading into the Northern
Hemisphere winter of 2026-27. In less mature markets, maintaining
volumes while passing on the higher fuel bill is more diﬃcult.
Airlines may also prioritise less fuel-eﬃcient, older-generation
aircraft over capacity growth.

### Page 11

Industry headwinds could become a catalyst for further
consolidation, ranging from minority stakes to full takeovers.
Fares could retreat if fuel prices ease, but
don't expect too much
Dynamic and algorithm-based pricing is becoming increasingly
common. This helps airlines optimise already historically high load
factors (84% in 2026 so far) but can also contribute to greater fare
volatility, especially as passengers book later amid uncertainty.
If fuel prices ease in 2027, fares could drop back. Yet relatively

strong demand, constrained aircraft availability and general
inﬂation mean a return to early-2026 fare levels looks unlikely.
Cargo beneﬁts from high-tech demand and
supply-chain volatility
Air cargo continues to perform well as a fast transport option in an
increasingly volatile and less predictable world. Volume growth
remained almost 5% year-to-date, while freight rates remained
attractive for carriers.
While e-commerce drove much of the growth in recent years,

digitalisation and large-scale AI investment increasingly support
shipments of high-value technology products. Strong cargo
performance helped cushion pressure on airline results in 2026.
European carriers also beneﬁted from reduced available freight
capacity from Middle Eastern competitors.
Freighter capacity received a boost during the pandemic through
passenger-to-freighter conversions, but that boost has largely run
its course. New-generation A350 and Boeing 777 freighters should

add capacity in the coming years.
Aircargo volume resilient in disruptive
geopolitical environment

Aviation’s centre of gravity is increasingly
shifting eastwards
The centre of gravity of global aviation is increasingly shifting
eastwards. Trips per capita are expected to see strong increases
over the next two decades, particularly in Asia. This matters even
more because these markets are far more populous.
Until recently, around 90% of the world’s population did not ﬂy in a
given year, but this is gradually changing. As a result, ﬂeet growth is

expected to be strongest in Asia, with its share of the global aircraft
ﬂeet increasing from around 33% to approximately 45%.

India is becoming a powerhouse for future
airline growth
Air travel is strongly correlated with GDP and household income. As
Asia’s middle class expands, the potential customer base for air
travel swells. For future aviation demand, this income eﬀect is even
more important than population growth alone.
Younger generations also appear keen to travel, adding to the
potential in countries such as India and Indonesia. Increasingly

internationally dispersed families provide another structural source
of demand.
India stands out here. Strong economic growth, rising household
incomes and a huge population oﬀer strong potential. Airlines are
positioning themselves accordingly, illustrated by historically large
aircraft orders from IndiGo and Air India. India’s aircraft ﬂeet is
expected to grow by around 8% annually on average over the next
two decades.

Supply-side developments
Aircraft scarcity keeps capacity tight and
lease rates elevated
Supply constraints have been curbing aviation growth since the
post-pandemic recovery and remain a major factor. The share of
stored aircraft dropped below 10% by the end of 2025, its lowest
level since 2019. Even several A380s (the largest aircraft) have
returned to service.
More than half of the global commercial aircraft ﬂeet is leased.

Tight capacity is consequently reﬂected in relatively high used-
aircraft values and lease rates.
Airbus and Boeing had a combined record backlog of around
15,000 aircraft by mid-2026. Production and deliveries continue to
lag order intake after seven consecutive years of subdued deliveries
from 2019 onwards. Demand for new-generation aircraft remains
strong, as illustrated by major recent orders from Avolon and
Turkish Airlines.
Production could ﬁnally return to pre-pandemic levels in 2027.

Chinese manufacturer COMAC, meanwhile, is making progress in
China in Asia, but Western certiﬁcation remains distant.

New airplane deliveries continue on a
recovery track now with Boeing rebounding
Number of delivered commercial airplanes by manufacturers Airbus &

Source: Company reports *Company forecast
Why aircraft supply remains constrained
Production has still not caught up with pre-pandemic levels
and is unlikely to do so in the next ﬁve years. Aircraft
manufacturing is recovering, but delays and large backlogs
push delivery dates into the 2030s. Airlines are therefore forced

to keep older aircraft ﬂying for longer.
Suppliers are still struggling to ramp up. Six years after the
sharp pandemic downturn, aviation supply chains have still
not fully normalised. Stringent safety and certiﬁcation
requirements mean manufacturers rely on a limited number of
specialised suppliers. Engines and sophisticated cabin
components still have long lead times, while skilled workers
remain scarce.
Engine issues continue to aﬀect available capacity. The peak

impact of the Pratt & Whitney inspection programme after an
identiﬁed production issue has passed, but checks and
maintenance continue to constrain parts of the A320neo-
family ﬂeet and absorb scarce maintenance capacity.

Orderbook Airbus & Boeing: number of commercial airplanes
Source: Company reports
Delivery catch-up is crucial for both
capacity and efﬁciency
New aircraft are critical not only to accommodate growth, but also
to improve eﬃciency. The average age of the global ﬂeet has
increased from around 13 to 15 years since 2019 due to production
constraints.
This matters increasingly as older units require more maintenance

at a time when skilled personnel and maintenance capacity are
scarce; they also consume signiﬁcantly more fuel and therefore
emit more.
Boeing is ﬁnally regaining altitude
supporting deliveries
Boeing is ﬁnally making a sustained comeback following an
unprecedented period of disruption stemming from the 737 MAX
accidents, the pandemic and subsequent production and quality
problems. It received certiﬁcation for its 737 MAX 7 and also the
737 MAX 10 recently. Boeing plans to increase production for the

family from 38 to 47 a month.

Higher 737 production should support deliveries in 2027 and
gradually bring pre-pandemic production levels back into sight. This
is hugely important for Boeing-dependent airlines such as Ryanair
and Southwest. Progress on certiﬁcation of the 777-9 is also
important for long-haul ﬂeet renewal.
Fleet renewal is currently the most
important decarbonisation lever
Air travel continues to grow, and associated emissions tend to
continue to rise further as well. Sustainable aviation fuels are

labelled as an important industry pathway to decarbonise, but
globally, blend rates still hover below 1% in 2026.
The closure of airspaces, too, has created ineﬃciencies and extra
emissions over the last few years, undermining gains elsewhere.
Around 63% of the global ﬂeet still consists of previous-generation
aircraft. Replacing them can reduce fuel consumption by 10-25% or
more, making ﬂeet renewal one of the most eﬀective near-term
decarbonisation levers available to airlines.

The challenge is to deliver proﬁtable growth
in a more disruptive world
For airlines, the challenge heading into 2027 is therefore not simply

ﬁnding suﬃcient demand. Relatively poor punctuality, with only
around 61% of ﬂights departing on time in 2026 year-to-date, is a
signal.
The globally operating industry faces more turbulence and
uncertainty amid intensiﬁed geopolitical risks. The challenge is to
deliver proﬁtable growth in a world of persistently constrained
capacity, higher costs and more frequent disruption.

Editorial 
Staying defensive and diversified  
Strategy summary:  Two weeks ago, we turned defensive 
towards equities, locking in semiconductor equity gains amid 
elevated bond volatility, narrowing market breadth and political 
uncertainty before the US mid -term elections. The near -term 
outlook reflected a less favourable risk-reward balance. Since 
we turned defensive , the Nasdaq 100 index has recorded its 
biggest weekly decline in three months as September’s hotter-
than-expected US inflation report briefly lifted bond yields. 
We have extended our defensive stance this week, 
downgrading US Communication Services equities to Neutral 
and upgrading US Healthcare to Overweight. We also closed 
our opportunistic bullish Communication Services idea and 
initiated a bullish idea on Healthcare, where earnings visibility 
and defensive characteristics appear more attractive. In fixed 
income, we see opportunities in US 10-year government bonds. 
We await clearer AI profit margins and spending guidance, 
broader earnings growth or lower bond and equity market 
volatility before turning positive on equities. Until then, 
diversification and disciplined entry levels remain important. 
Hot US inflation triggers equity pullback; not hot enough 
for an October Fed hike:  Risk assets pulled back after 
September’s hotter-than-expected inflation data (headline 3.7% 
y/y; core 2.6% y/y). Higher gasoline and diesel prices were the 
main drivers, but passthrough appeared in airline fares, used 
cars and transportation services, showing pressures were not 
confined to energy. Almost half of inflation components are still 
rising above 3%, a measure recently cited by Fed Chair Warsh. 
Producer inflation also beat estimates. The reports revive the 
possibility of an October Fed rate hike, but we expect a divided 
Fed to weigh it against September’s soft jobs report and 
narrowly hold this month. A December hike appears more likely 
if inflation remains firm . Although Fed Chair Warsh did not 
comment on policy at an IMF speech this week, New York Fed 
chief Williams said he saw no need to hike in 2027. Our base 
case remains two further hikes by June 2027. 
Limited equity pullback so far.  Equities fell sharply after the 
US inflation report, but the pullback is limited. The Nasdaq 100 
is 4.5% below its record high, while the S&P 500 remains close 
to all -time highs despite the latest decline. The S&P 500 
volatility index (VIX) has risen from below 15 to 1 8.2, still well 
under the 25 –30 range typically associated with capitulation 
and forced selling. Meanwhile, US government bond volatility 
(MOVE) remains elevated after surging since September.  Our 
stock-bond quant model turned more negativ e (-2) this week, 
signalling elevated equity volatility in the near term.  
When to turn more constructive on stocks?  We would turn 
more constructive when capitulation signals align: the Nasdaq 
100 approaches a 10% drawdown, the VIX rises to 25 –30 and 
our ‘Fear and Greed’ index  enters “extreme fear”. Greater 
confidence would also require easing concerns about AI 
spending and technology firms’ exposure to neocloud revenue, 
lower bond volatility and our stock-bond model turning positive 
again. Until these conditions emerge, volatility may remain 
elevated, favouring a defensive equity stance. Political risk 
should ease after the US mid -term elections. We continue to 
seek selective opportunities following excessive corrections. 
US financials remain a preferred sector after Q3 earnings:  
US large banks’ earnings were mixed, but underlying trends 
remain encouraging. Healthy loan and deposit growth supports 
net interest income, while resilient consumer spending, wealth 
management activity and a solid M&A and refinancing pipeline 
strengthen the outlook. Credit risks appear manageable . We 
remain constructive and favour stronger, diversified franchises. 
US government bonds offer value as yields spike:  The 
reversal in US government bond yields after their initial inflation-
driven spike suggests limited further upside. The 10 -year yield 
briefly reached 5.32% before slumping as falling equities 
prompted short-covering. We expect a near -term 5.00–5.25% 
range and view moves above 5.25% as attractive entry points 
for our opportunistic 10-year government bond idea. Structural 
pressures, including term premium and increasing supply to 
fund fiscal deficits and AI investments, prevent us from turning 
outright bullish on longer maturities. We, therefore, continue to 
prefer 3–7-year maturities in broader bond allocations.  
—  Rajat Bhattacharya and Sundeep Gantori

Top client questions 
  How does the September 2026 US Consumer Price Index 
(CPI) report alter your view on the USD and bond yields?   
Our view: The hotter-than-expected CPI print raises the odds of 
an October Fed hike, though we still expect a hold followed by 
a rate hike in December. In the near term, we maintain our view 
that the US 10 -year government bond yield will range between 
5.00% and 5.25%, while  the USD will remain supported as 
markets reassess the likelihood of further Fed hikes. Additional 
gains would depend partly on markets pricing a faster or more 
prolonged tightening cycle, while clearer signs of an 
approaching policy rate peak could see the USD ease back. 
Rationale: September US consumer inflation  came in above 
consensus across the board – headline CPI rose 3.7% y/y (vs. 3.6% 
estimate), and core CPI rose 2.6% y/y (vs. 2.5% estimate) – marking 
the fastest headline acceleration in five months. This shifts the 
balance of risks modestly hawkish . Unsurprisingly, the market -
implied probability of an October Fed hike rose over 50% overnight 
but closed the day at 32.7% – 9ppt higher than Tuesday’s close. 
We believe a split Fed will weigh this inflation report against the soft 
September jobs report and narrowly vote to keep rates on hold this 
month. Our base case remains for two more Fed hikes  by June 
2027. A December rate hike  now looks more like a done deal, 
especially as persistently higher oil prices keep headline and core 
inflation elevated for at least the next few months. Any re-escalation 
of the Middle East conflict after the  US mid-term elections would 
exert pressure on the Fed, although we believe Republicans would  
show greater restraint in US foreign action if they suffer steep Senate 
losses, which looks increasingly likely. 
The intra-day price action in US government bonds was instructive. 
The US 10-year yield briefly spiked to 5.32% on the print before 
closing materially lower, as pre -existing bearish positioning was 
unwound and Fed speakers (Barkin, Goolsbee) stopped well short 
of signalling an imminent move. This dynamic reinforces our view 
that the technical selling pressure driving yields towards the upper 
end of our range is fading. Structural drivers – term premium, fiscal 
supply concerns and ‘higher for longer’ Fed repricing – remain intact 
and keep us from turning outright bullish on duration. However, our 
opportunistic bullish idea in US 10-year government bonds initiated 
at September-end remains, as we continue to view spikes in US 10-
year yields over 5.25% as a good risk-reward entry. From a longer-
term portfolio standpoint, we continue to favour the 3-7-year tenor. 
On FX, elevated US government bond yields should sustain the 
USD’s interest rate appeal. However, expected hikes alone will not 
drive further appreciation. Stronger data or firmer Fed guidance 
would provide fresh support, while evidence that tightening is 
nearing completion would temper the USD’s strength. 
—  Vincent Tan, Senior Investment Strategist 
— Ray Heung, Senior Investment Strategist

Top client questions (cont’d) 
  What are your key takeaways from US bank earnings? 
Our view: Q3 2026 earnings results from major US banks have 
been mixed, but underlying trends remain encouraging. Healthy 
loan and deposit growth, resilient consumer spending and 
wealth management activity continue to support the sector. 
Credit risks remain manageable. We remain constructive on the 
US financial sector, favouring stronger, diversified franchises. 
Rationale: Healthy loan and deposit growth continue to support net 
interest income (NII), hinting that the US economy remains resilient. 
Capital markets revenue grew year -on-year (y/y) , but moderated 
sequentially after a very strong Q2 2026, although performance 
varied across banks. Management commentary points to a healthy 
deal pipeline , supported by M&A activity and debt refinancing 
demand, although execution will depend on market conditions. 
Provisioning and net charge -off trends were mixed across banks, 
with no clear signs of broad deterioration in credit quality. Firmer 
US inflation raises the risk of further monetary tightening. While 
higher rates can support asset yields, they can also increase 
funding costs, pressure borrowers and weigh on securities ’ 
valuations. We will continue to monitor lending demand, credit 
costs, NII trends, capital markets momentum and capital returns.  
—  Robin Xie, Senior Investment Strategist 
  Can Big Tech’s earnings guidance sustain confidence in 
the AI investment cycle? 
Our view: We expect Big Tech’s AI spending to remain elevated, 
supporting our constructive AI capex outlook. However, we 
await guidance on the pace of capex growth and the 
sustainability of profit margins. 
Rationale: Semiconductor leaders’ latest company guidance points 
to supply constraints extending through 2028, supporting continued 
capacity expansion for compute . However, while AI capex is still 
likely to rise, y/y growth is expected to moderate  from c.100% in 
Q3 2026 to c.20% in Q3 2027. This normalisation in growth could 
raise concerns about the AI investment cycle’s durability.  
The Nasdaq-100 Index has rallied alongside accelerating AI capex. 
Slower capex growth is likely to moderate semiconductor revenue 
growth, while hyperscalers continue to incur depreciation costs on 
past investments. The slower growth is already partially reflected in 
the Nasdaq -100’s valuation de -rating this year. While we remain 
constructive on the AI investment theme, we prefer to stay 
prudent in the near term and await Big Tech’s guidance for greater 
visibility into spending plans in H2 2027 and beyond. 
—  Ryan Goh, Investment Strategist

Top client questions (cont’d) 
  Would France face a credit rating downgrade by rating 
agencies this month? What might be the market implications? 
Our view: A rating downgrade is unlikely unless France’s 2027 
budget passes the National Assembly very soon with material 
changes to the proposal. We see French government bond 
yields remaining elevated relative to German Bund yields. 
Rationale: The French National Assembly began debating France’s 
2027 draft budget on 13 October 2026, with the first vote scheduled 
for 20 October. Near-term budget approval appears unlikely, as 
opposition parties have tabled motions to reject the proposal. The 
French Parliament has up to 70 days from the budget’s submission 
to complete the legislative process, although  its final adoption and 
the resolution of political challenges could extend into early 2027.  
Last October, two of the three major rating agencies downgraded 
France by one notch to the high-single-A category  with stable 
outlooks. The remaining agenc y rated France in the low-AA 
category with a negative outlook. As negative outlooks are typically 
resolved within 12 -18 months, agenc ies have time to await fiscal 
clarity before acting. We believe downgrade risks are largely priced 
in after the recent rise in yields, but volatility is likely to persist amid 
fiscal uncertainty and the approaching presidential election. Banks 
and domestically-focused issuers would face the greatest near-term 
pressure. However, we would view wider spreads as an opportunity 
to add exposure, particularly to French banks’ subordinated 
debt, given their stronger balance sheets and the fact that France 
contributes less than 50% of major French banks’ overall revenue. 
—  Ray Heung, Senior Investment Strategist 
  Are you still positive on Japanese banks? 
Our view: We are positive on Japanese banks despite the recent 
market correction, as the structural drivers of improving 
profitability and shareholder returns remain intact . While 
political risk and shifting BoJ rate hike odds could sustain near-
term volatility, we see the recent pullback as an opportunity to 
build selective exposure to Japanese bank stocks. 
Rationale: Japan’s gradual monetary policy normalisation  
should support banks’ NII as floating-rate loans reprice and maturing 
assets are reinvested at higher yields. Healthy corporate lending 
demand, improving capital efficiency and continued share buybacks 
provide further support . While uncertainty over the pace of BoJ 
tightening could weigh on sentiment, we see gradual interest rate 
normalisation as supportive of medium-term bank profitability.  
Key risks  include rising deposit costs, mark -to-market losses on 
bond portfolios and a disorderly increase in Japanese government 
bond yields. We continue to favour well-capitalised banks  with 
strong domestic deposit franchises and improving returns on equity. 
—  Robin Xie, Senior Investment Strategist

Top client questions (cont’d) 
  Could NZD/USD rebound from its one-year trough? If so, 
how far could it recover?  
Our view: New Zealand’s improving domestic conditions, 
persistent inflation and technical support provide a basis for 
NZD/USD’s initial recovery towards the 0.57 level, although 
elevated US bond yields could slow its progress. 
Rationale: In Q3, New Zealand’s  seasonally-adjusted business 
confidence reading rose to a net 40% of firms expecting the economy 
to improve, up from net 14% in Q2 . Hiring intentions improved, and 
filled jobs rose 0.2% m/m in August. These developments suggest 
domestic conditions remain supportive for the NZD.  
New Zealand’s above-target inflation keeps further RBNZ tightening 
in focus. The 22 October consumer inflation data release and the 
28 October RBNZ policy meeting are key catalysts: persistent price 
pressures a nd improving demand are expected to prompt firmer 
policy guidance and strengthen the NZD’s interest-rate appeal. 
NZD/USD’s position near the lower boundary of its downtrend 
channel suggests scope for a technical rebound. We see 0.57 as 
the first recovery hurdle; a sustained break  above this level  would 
strengthen the case for further gains. Firmer US  consumer inflation 
remains a headwind, making a gradual recovery more plausible 
than a sharp reversal.  
—  Vincent Tan, Senior Investment Strategist 
—  Iris Yuen, Investment Strategist 
  Can the proposed Russia -Ukraine ‘energy ceasefire ’ 
contain oil prices as Middle East risks rise? 
Our view: We expect escalating Middle East tensions to keep oil 
prices elevated . We  maintain our  three- and 12 -month West 
Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price forecasts at USD 100/bbl and 
USD 80/bbl, respectively, and continue to favour US Treasury 
Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) as a portfolio hedge 
against persistent inflation risks. 
Rationale: The proposed Russia-Ukraine ‘energy ceasefire’ still 
looks some way off. In our view, even if an agreement is reached, it 
would do little to ease the supply risks building in the Middle East. 
Gulf oil exports have recovered to above 80% of pre-conflict levels 
in recent weeks, helping moderate the pace of price increases. 
However, the recovery remains vulnerable to disruptions, particularly 
following the latest Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure . 
Diesel and jet fuel remain under the most pressure , with Gulf 
exports of these fuels in September  at only around 60% of pre -
conflict levels. A sustained disruption to major Saudi production or 
export infrastructure remains the principal upside risk to oil prices. 
—  Anthony Naab, Investment Strategist

### Page 1

The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc.
Global bond yields have risen to multi-decade highs, yet growth and markets have
remained remarkably resilient. But with some pressures beginning to emerge (e.g. in
European sovereign bond markets), can this resilience last, or will more vulnerabilities
be revealed? We ask the IMF’s Tobias Adrian, Moody’s Analytics’ Mark Zandi, and GS
economists. Adrian is relatively sanguine about the economy’s resilience, though
notes downside risks, while GS economists expect only a modest growth drag from

higher rates, but a more consequential one if yields remain near current or higher
levels. Zandi is generally more concerned, describing the US economy as vulnerable
rather than resilient, and sees one-in-three odds of the economy going off the rails.
Meanwhile, GS strategists and analysts are not especially concerned about banks or
markets more broadly, but warn that further increases in yields or rate volatility could
test risk assets. Key to watch: whether the increasingly interconnected and leveraged

AI investment boom can continue to withstand higher rates.
Tobias Adrian, Special Advisor and former Director of Monetary and Capital Markets, IMF
“The global economy has demonstrated considerable resilience in the face of multiple severe shocks, and I would not be
surprised if it continues to shrug off higher yields, provided they do not keep rising sharply in a disorderly fashion. At the same
time, I do worry about downside risks.”
Mark Zandi, Chief Economist, Moody’s Analytics
